rules.title: NJ Law Against Discrimination – source of lawful income protection
rules.requirement: Landlords may not discriminate in housing based on the source of lawful income or the source of lawful rent payment a tenant uses. For example, a landlord cannot deny an apartment to a Section 8 voucher holder based solely on that source of income.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rentals of all real property in New Jersey, residential or business, subject to the LAD's limited exceptions.
rules.exemptions: Rental of one unit in an owner-occupied two-family dwelling. Rental of rooms in a one-family dwelling occupied by the owner or occupant as a residence. Religious-organization preference for persons of the same religion. Familial-status protection does not apply to housing for older persons.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Exempt if a two-family dwelling where the owner occupies the other unit, or a room rental in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling.

rules.penalty: Complaint to the Division on Civil Rights within 180 days, or to NJ Superior Court within two years of the violation.
rules.citation: New Jersey Law Against Discrimination, N.J.S.A. 10:5-1 et seq.
rules.quoted_span:
The LAD also prohibits housing discrimination  based
on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent
or mortgage payment a tenant or purchaser uses.
rules.conflict_note: Brochure (rev. 2015) does not give the specific section or effective date of the source-of-income provision. The citation is to the LAD generally.
